title: Analysis and Design Optimization of a Coaxial Surface-Mounted Permanent-Magnet Magnetic Gear

source.citation: X. Zhang, X. Liu, C. Wang, Z. Chen, Energies 7(12):8535-8553, 2014

machine.topology: coaxial radial-flux magnetic gear: inner PM rotor, a stationary ring of modulating pole pieces, outer PM rotor; surface magnets filling the pole pitch
machine.poles: 2 x 23 outer, 2 x 4 inner (base); variants 11/2 to 28/5
machine.symmetry: Full cross-section (the combinations have no common periodicity). Two sliding bands, one in each air gap; the inner band turns the inner rotor.

components_map.part: outer and inner PM rings (magnets fill the pole pitch, radially magnetized)
modulating pole pieces with air between them

components_map.component: waveform_statistic assessor (fundamental over the inner rotor's period)

outer_diameter_mm.quote: outer diameter of the magnetic gear 320 mm

stack_length_mm.note: The 2D model's depth; end effects are neglected, as the analytic model assumes.

outer_pole_pairs.note: p_o of the outer PM ring.

inner_pole_pairs.note: p_i of the inner PM ring.

piece_width_ratio.note: tau_m/tau_p. The analytic model's slots are angular sectors (Fig. 2, Equation (28)), so this is the pole pieces' angular share of their pitch.

piece_length_ratio.note: tau_l/tau_p: radial length over the pole-piece pitch (gap: at which radius).

outer_magnet_mm.quote: thickness of the outer PM ring 6 mm

inner_magnet_mm.quote: thickness of the inner PM ring 6 mm

outer_gap_mm.quote: length of the outer air-gap 1 mm

inner_gap_mm.quote: length of the inner air-gap 1 mm

magnet_mu_r.quote: Relative recoil permeability of PM is 1;
magnet_mu_r.note: The analytic model's assumption; the paper's FEM recoil permeability is not stated.

iron_material.note: Linear iron of iron_mu_r stands for infinite permeability; control nonlinear-steel builds the iron of M-19 to compare with the paper's nonlinear FEM.

iron_mu_r.reason: Stands for the analytic model's infinitely permeable iron; control iron-mu-1e5.

pitch_depth_fraction.reason: Where tau_p is measured for tau_l: 0 at the pole pieces' outer face R4, 0.5 at their mean radius, 1 at R3. Table 2's PM masses fix 0: with it the implied magnet density varies 0.28-0.44% across the six pole-pair combinations, against 1.3-2.6% at the mean radius or R3 (geometry check 1).

yoke_arc_depth_fraction.reason: Where 'the arc width of the PM block' is measured for the yoke thickness: 0 at the face against the yoke, 0.5 at the magnet's mean radius. The steel masses of Tables 1-3 favour 0.5 (spread 0.76% against 2.0%, geometry check 2); with infinitely permeable iron the yoke only sets the radial build.

band_margin_mm.reason: Each sliding band lies 0.3 mm inside its 1 mm gap, leaving thin air rings on both faces.

thin_air_mesh_mm.reason: Air between a ring face and its sliding band.

gap_arc_deg.reason: Arcs at and next to the gaps (0.65 mm at 150 mm).

piece_mesh_mm.reason: Pole pieces and the air between them.

positions_per_period.reason: Inner rotor positions over one electrical period (15 electrical degrees apart).

r7_mm.note: Outer surface of the outer yoke.

r6_mm.note: Outer yoke thickness is half the outer PM's arc width (pi/p_o of arc), measured yoke_arc_depth_fraction into the magnet.

r4_mm.note: Outer face of the pole pieces.

piece_length_mm.note: tau_l = ratio times the pole-piece pitch, taken pitch_depth_fraction of tau_l inside R4.

r0_mm.note: Inner yoke thickness, as for the outer yoke.

gaps.item: the radius at which the pole-piece pitch tau_p is taken for tau_l/tau_p
gaps.affects: every radius inside the outer gap, hence every torque
gaps.note: At the pole pieces' outer face R4: Table 2's PM masses imply a magnet density constant within 0.28-0.44% across six designs at R4, against 1.3-2.6% elsewhere (geometry check 1). Control pitch-at-mean-radius.

gaps.item: where the PM 'arc width' is measured for the yoke thickness
gaps.note: At the magnet's mean radius, favoured by the steel masses (geometry check 2). Control yoke-arc-at-yoke-face.

gaps.item: how the stall torque is read from the torque curve
gaps.note: As the paper defines it ('the maximum point of the outer rotor torque curve', p. 8543): the largest of 24 samples over one electrical period of the inner rotor. The sweep starts where the torque is zero by symmetry, so the peak falls on a sample, a quarter period later. Frozen first (commit c7da1b5) as the fundamental amplitude, on the assumption that the curve is sinusoidal; run1 showed a third harmonic of 3% of the fundamental, so the fundamental read 3% below the maximum. The procedure was corrected after run1, whose article level is kept.

gaps.item: the steel and the recoil permeability of the paper's FEM
gaps.note: Not stated; the FEM values are comparators. Control nonlinear-steel builds the iron of M-19 for the base design.

gaps.item: the orientation of the rotors at the start of the sweep
gaps.affects: nothing measured: the sweep covers a whole electrical period
gaps.note: Outer magnet 0 and pole piece 0 are centred at 0 degrees, inner magnet 0 likewise; the stall torque is a property of the period.

coverage.reproduced: Analytic stall torque of the outer rotor for the initial design, the five other pole-pair combinations of Table 2 and the five optimized designs of Table 3, and the inner rotor's stall torque of the initial design; the paper's FEM stall torques as comparators.
coverage.not_reproduced: The air-gap flux density plots (Figs. 3-4), the parameter sweeps (Figs. 6-8), the PSO optimization itself, costs and torque densities (derived from the same torques).
